title: Prompt Engineering
excerpt: Lilian Weng catalogs prompt engineering techniques from zero-shot and few-shot prompting through chain-of-thought, self-consistency, and tool-augmented workflows for LLMs. The survey predates agent-native frameworks and focuses on prompting patterns rather than benchmarked head-to-head comparisons.
author: Lilian Weng

title: Learning with Not Enough Data Part 3: Data Generation & Active Learning
excerpt: Lilian Weng explains active learning loops, uncertainty sampling, and synthetic data generation when labeled data is scarce, connecting classical ML sample-efficiency ideas to modern deep learning practice. Examples skew toward vision and classification rather than LLM fine-tuning at scale.
author: Lilian Weng

title: How to Train Really Large Models on Many GPUs?
excerpt: Lilian Weng surveys parallelism strategies—data, tensor, pipeline, and optimizer sharding—for training large neural networks across many GPUs, with diagrams of ZeRO-style partitioning and communication trade-offs. The post is architectural overview rather than a reproducible cluster recipe for a specific stack.
author: Lilian Weng

title: Making LLM Embeddings Work for You
excerpt: Simon Willison demonstrates practical patterns for LLM embeddings—semantic search, clustering, and lightweight RAG—using concrete CLI and Python examples developers can run locally. The tooling landscape has evolved since 2023, but the embedding workflow patterns remain widely applicable.
author: Simon Willison
